html:
The Karajarri are an Aboriginal Australian people of Western Australia, living south of Broome between the coast and the Great Sandy Desert. The map shows them from 1600 to 1815. Most now live at Bidyadanga, a community that began as the La Grange Catholic mission, south of Broome.

Their neighbours were the Yawuru to the north, the Mangala to the east, the Nyikina to the northeast and the Nyangumarta to the south, with the Djugun on the coast near Broome. Their coast, with its long tidal flats, gave them fish and shellfish, while the inland sandhill country was hunting ground. In 2002 they became one of the first peoples in Western Australia to have native title recognised.
